subject: Burst ramp verification & demo schedule
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@fleetops.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 15:04:00 +0000
Subject: Burst ramp verification & demo schedule

Hi Ryan / Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery on the performance and SLO constraints you shared, and proposed next steps so we can validate before procurement: 

Key SLOs & workload characteristics (as discussed)
- P95 latency target: <= 120ms for chat responses (end-to-end, from request arrival to first token streamed)
- Sustained throughput: ~200 req/s (75% of traffic is short prompts ~40–80 tokens)
- Concurrency: expected spikes up to 70 concurrent streams during morning batch jobs (30–90s windows)
- Streaming requirements: partial response streaming required (first token <= 120ms; steady streaming at ~15–25 tokens/sec)
- Acceptable scale-up window for burst events: prefer <90s to reach target concurrency; ideal <60s for critical flows
- Queueing: prefer graceful queueing with prioritized warm-pool-backed requests (no hard 503s for customer-facing routes)

Proposed verification plan (attached: FleetOps-MAP-20270518.xlsx, sample-load-config.json):
1) We run an internal ramp demo against a staging replica of your traffic pattern (we'll use the sample-load-config).
2) Measure P50/P95/P99 and token-stream start time under an induced burst to 250 req/s for 3 minutes.
3) Validate scale-up time with a warm-pool of N GPUs (we discussed 3–5); Dev will recommend optimal pool size.
4) Confirm queueing behavior and fallback policy during saturation; we can enable model-fallback + queued priority for critical routes.

Ask: can you confirm the demo window below (we'll provision a warm pool in advance):
- Proposed demo: Thursday, May 20, 2027, 16:00–17:00 PT / 23:00–00:00 UTC

If that works, we'll share a short pre-demo checklist: sample prompts, expected token lengths, and a baseline perf CSV for you to review. 

Thanks — I'll loop in Dev and Ben to coordinate the technical plan.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: FleetOps-MAP-20270518.xlsx (xlsx), sample-load-config.json (json), perf-baseline.csv (csv)

From: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@fleetops.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sarah Lim <sarah.lim@fleetops.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Burst ramp verification & demo schedule

Thanks Vanessa — this recap looks right. A couple of tweaks from our side before the demo: 

- Concurrency detail: the 70 concurrent streams is accurate for peak, but during billing cutover we could see a thin spike to ~110 for <30s. Can the test include a short "super-spike" stage to 110 concurrent?
- Streaming requirement: we need deterministic first-token latency for the first 3 tokens (important for our UI). Please include those metrics explicitly.
- Warm-pool preference: Ops prefers 4 GPUs in the warm pool for the demo (we can temporarily increase if you recommend it).

Thursday 20 May at 16:00 PT works for our team. We'll send the sample prompt set and a list of critic cases (long-context messages) by tomorrow morning.

One request on reporting: include a CSV with per-request timelines (arrival, scale event, first-token, last-token, model used) so we can map to our tracing.

Appreciate the fast follow-up.

—Ryan
Ryan Cole | Head of Platform Engineering, FleetOps
ryan.cole@fleetops.com

Team — forwarding Ryan's confirmation and small changes. Short asks: can we confirm the warm-pool sizing guidance and build the test harness for the super-spike (110 concurrent for 30s)? Vanessa, Ryan said he will send critic cases tomorrow.

High level notes for the eng plan:
- Baseline run: 200 req/s steady for 3m
- Super-spike: ramp to 110 concurrent (mix of streaming + short prompts) for 30s
- Measure: first-token (ms), p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, time-to-target-concurrency, and tail queue length during scale-up

Attachments: scale-sim-plan.md (md) — contains the simulated load profile and test harness commands. Dev, can you review and add the exact warm-pool GPU counts and expected scale timings? We need an answer by EOD PT so we can reserve cloud capacity.

Thanks,
Ben

ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ryan Cole <ryan.cole@fleetops.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 18:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Burst ramp verification & demo schedule — technical plan and checklist

Hi Ryan / Sarah / Vanessa —

Thanks — we've sketched a technical plan and can support the demo Thursday 20 May 16:00 PT. Summary of what we'll run and what to expect: 

Technical plan (short):
- Warm pool: provision 4 NVIDIA A10s as requested. We will also snapshot a 6-GPU pool as a backstop (no billing changes for the demo).
- Baseline run: run 200 req/s for 3 minutes against the staging endpoint (model pinned to open-compat variant). Collect per-request timeline and streaming timestamps.
- Super-spike stage: at t+4m, inject a 30s spike to 110 concurrent streams. We'll randomly select 20% long-context critic cases to stress KV cache behavior.
- Metrics captured: first-token latency, per-token throughput, p50/p95/p99 end-to-end, model-variant fallback events, time-to-target-concurrency (measured from first queueing event), and queue length/time-to-drain.

Pre-demo checklist for FleetOps (please provide prior to the run):
- Sample prompt set + critic cases (attach as .csv) — we need expected token lengths and which ones must be prioritized.
- Expected routing: which route(s) should be marked high-priority vs best-effort.
- Any IP ranges for staging to whitelist (if needed).

Expected results guidance (what success looks like):
- First-token: <= 120ms for 95% of prioritized requests during steady-state; super-spike may see 120–300ms for non-prioritized routes while priority routes remain under 200ms.
- Time to reach 110 concurrent: ~55–85s depending on queue build and cold start; with the warm pool we expect ~60s median to target.
- Queueing behavior: prioritized routes will be admitted preferentially; lower-priority requests will be queued up to 60s before backpressure responses if necessary.

We will push the following artifacts to the Drive link before the demo:
- perf-baseline.csv (per-request sample)
- sample-load-config.json (load generator config)
- a short runbook for the demo and rollback steps

Meeting link: https://meet.google.com/xyz-demo (we'll host)
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3-example
Jira (tracking): https://redwood-inference.atlassian.net/browse/RDW-4721

If that aligns with your expectations, Vanessa — please confirm and we will provision the warm pool tonight.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Principal Engineer, Inference Runtimes | Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: perf-baseline.csv (csv), sample-load-config.json (json)
